summary: This lecture from Zadul-Ma'ad Part 96 discusses the stages and significance of Hijra (migration) in Islamic history. Sheikh Ali Mashhour explains the three phases of migration: the first small group migration to Abyssinia (about 16 people), the second migration (approximately 83 companions), and the third general migration from Mecca to Medina. The lecture clarifies that migration was permitted to escape persecution—both direct bodily harm and infringement of religious and civil rights. It emphasizes that migration was obligatory only from Mecca where persecution was unbearable, while Muslims in other regions could remain if they could freely practice Islam. The speaker introduces the concept of Al-Muhadramun (those who accepted Islam but didn't migrate to meet the Prophet), explaining how Islam spread through these believers returning to their tribes. The lecture also extensively discusses the Battle of Badr participants and their exceptional virtue, noting that no hypocrites participated in Badr unlike subsequent battles, and that Badr fighters had no worldly incentives, making them purely faithful believers promised paradise.
